research_rationale: EO 7814 (signed 1938-02-15, 3 FR 447) is a one-time land action: it revokes EO 4430 of April 23, 1926, as modified, "as to the following-described public land" (Fourth Principal Meridian, T. 32 N., R. 9 W., sec. 9, lot 1, .50 of an acre). The dossier's single clause covered the neighboring National Wild Life Week proclamation text (characters 0-2585), not the order, so the inventory is corrected to the order's operative text at characters 2990-3475 of the held Federal Register page. The revocation is self-executing ("is hereby revoked") and was performed when the order was signed on 1938-02-15; it is a completed act, not a continuing duty (completion_of_task). Later, EO 8861 (1941-08-20; 6 FR 4289) revoked EO 4430 as a whole, so the parent withdrawal that EO 7814 had partly lifted no longer exists and nothing remains for EO 7814 to modify. EO 8861 does not name EO 7814, so EO 7814 itself has not been formally revoked; the 1989 OFR row 'Revoked by EO 8861' is an editorial reading. The first end rests on the order's own self-executing terms, with EO 8861 (1941-08-20) as the latest possible bound. Status proposal: no.
savings_reason: The release of the 0.50-acre lot from the EO 4430 withdrawal accrued on 1938-02-15 under the order's own words; the surviving consequence is the land's released status, which EO 7814 requires no further action to maintain.
earlier_end_check: Searched held texts for EO 7814's number (Cruden regex): the only hit is a derivative formulario table that lists EO 7814 as amending EO 4430, with no revocation entry. The dossier chain has no events; the only later instrument is EO 8861 (parent revoked 1941-08-20). The first end is the order's own performance on 1938-02-15, earlier than any later revocation, which is treated as a bound/disposition and not as the first end.
scope_check: EO 7814 revokes EO 4430 only 'as to' one described 0.50-acre lot; the clause is limited to that lot. EO 8861 revokes EO 4430 in full, which also covers the rest of the withdrawal, so no part of EO 4430 depends on EO 7814.
independent_command_check: There is one command (partial revocation as to one lot); it has no deadline, report or continuing duty. The surviving effect is the released status of that lot.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued per the accrued 1938 release; the order's own text is the source.

research_rationale: EO 9446 (signed 1944-06-08, effective 1944-07-01 by its own terms; 9 FR 6293) prescribed five paragraphs of regulations on travel-expense allowances for Veterans' Administration claimants, beneficiaries and attendants under the act of March 14, 1940 (54 Stat. 49). Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (signed 1948-07-07; 13 FR 3805, held in the Federal Register printing) states "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944" and re-prescribes regulations on the same subject. EO 9975 states no later effective date, so it took effect on signing, 1948-07-07; all five clauses of EO 9446 ended then by express supersession. A search of the held texts for the number 9446 finds only EO 9975 (and a duplicate printing page) as later instruments; the dossier chain records the single supersession. Status proposal: no.
savings_reason: EO 9975 re-prescribes regulations on the allowance of travel expenses of Veterans' Administration claimants, beneficiaries and attendants and again authorises the Administrator to prescribe implementing rules, so the subject continues under the successor order; EO 9446's own paragraphs have no residual independent command.
earlier_end_check: Searched held texts for the number 9446: only EO 9975 (and the same Federal Register page printing of EO 9447's page) cite it; no earlier revocation, amendment or own-terms end. The order's own terms contain no expiry; the 'effective July 1, 1944' sentence is a start date, not an end.
scope_check: Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 supersedes EO 9446 as a whole, not a part, and EO 9975 replaces the subject matter of all five paragraphs.
independent_command_check: Paragraphs 1-4 are standing allowance rules and paragraph 5 is a standing rule-making authority; none is a one-time command or a deadline, and each ended with the supersession.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued: the successor order covers the same subject; no accrued rights are claimed beyond that.

research_rationale: EO 8875 (signed 1941-08-28, 6 FR 4483) delegated priority powers to the Office of Production Management (OPM) (paragraphs 1, 2, 4, 6, 7), created the Supply Priorities and Allocations Board (SPAB) (paragraphs 3, 5), renamed the Office of Price Administration and Civilian Supply (8), limited its reach (9), abolished the OPM Priorities Board (10) and amended/rescinded conflicting provisions of EO 8629 and EO 8734 (11). EO 9024 (signed 1942-01-16; 7 FR 329) says "is hereby abolished, and its personnel, records, and property transferred to the Board." of the SPAB, so the SPAB clauses (3, 4, 5) ended on 1942-01-16; it also gives the War Production Board chairman SPAB's powers under EO 8875 and leaves OPM in being under the chairman's supervision. EO 9040 (signed 1942-01-24; 7 FR 527) provides that OPM "is abolished and its personnel, records, property, and funds are transferred to the War" Production Board and that the Chairman performs OPM's functions, so the OPM clauses (1, 2, 6, 7) and the order's reach limit (9) ended on 1942-01-24, the latest clause end and the whole-order end. Paragraphs 8, 10 and 11 are self-executing one-time acts completed on signing 1941-08-28. The dossier segmentation splits paragraph 1 at the odd scope 'EO:8875#1941' (the rest of 1(b)-(d)); the two scopes together are paragraph 1, and the inventory is otherwise complete (paragraphs 1-11). Both later orders have no later effective-date clause, so signing dates are used. Status proposal: no.
savings_reason: EO 9024 transfers SPAB's personnel, records, property and functions under EO 8875 to the War Production Board, and EO 9040 transfers OPM's functions, personnel, records, property and funds to the War Production Board, so the priorities functions continued with the successor body; nothing in EO 8875 survives as an independent command.
earlier_end_check: Searched held texts for the number 8875: EO 8942 (1941-11-19; builds on OPM powers, an amendment/extension, not an end), EO 9024 and a reference list in EO 9005 are the only citations. EO 9024 (1942-01-16) ended the SPAB clauses; no earlier end of the OPM clauses is shown, since EO 9024 leaves OPM in existence and EO 9040 abolishes it on 1942-01-24. The 'Offices abolished by EOs 9024, 9040' 1989 note agrees.
scope_check: EO 9024's general sentence that conflicting provisions are superseded is not used as a blanket end; each clause is ended by the specific abolition of the body it commands (SPAB by EO 9024, OPM by EO 9040), or by its own self-executing terms (paragraphs 8, 10, 11).
independent_command_check: Paragraph 8 (rename), 10 (abolish the Priorities Board) and 11 (amend/rescind) are one-time self-executing commands, separated from the standing delegations; paragraph 9 is a construction limit on the order's powers and ends with the last such power on 1942-01-24; nothing in them outlives the order.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued per EO 9024 and EO 9040 transfers of functions, records and property to the War Production Board.

research_rationale: EO 10733 (signed 1957-10-10, 22 FR 8135) does nothing but amend section 3 of EO 10479, which created the Government Contract Committee: it changes the preamble's "fifteen" to "sixteen" members and rewrites paragraph (b) to add an Executive Vice Chairman. Section 403 of EO 10925 (signed 1961-03-06; 26 FR 1977), whose text is held, names EO 10479, EO 10482, EO 10733 "(22 F.R. 8135)" and EO 10557, declares them "hereby revoked" and abolishes the Committee; section 402 makes EO 10925 effective thirty days after its execution, i.e. 1961-04-05 (the exclusive reading of 'thirty days after' is the same day). A Cruden regex search of the held texts for the number 10733 finds no later instrument other than EO 10925; the 1989 OFR table also records 'Revoked by EO 10925'. Both clauses of the order are therefore terminated on 1961-04-05 and the whole order ends on that date. Status proposal: no.
savings_reason: Section 403 of EO 10925 transfers all records and property of the Committee to the President's Committee on Equal Employment Opportunity, which winds up the Committee's outstanding affairs; no continuing independent command of EO 10733 survives, because the amendment's only subject (membership of the abolished Committee) is gone.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts for the number 10733 (the packet number lookup matches nothing because EO 10925 prints the number inside a list; a Cruden regex search for 'Nos./Orders ... 10733' finds only the order's own printings and an unrelated '35 FR 10733' page, besides EO 10925 section 403 which I read directly) and read the dossier chain (no events) and the 1989 OFR row (Revoked by EO 10925). No earlier revocation, own-terms end or statute expiry is shown; the amended EO 10479 itself was ended by EO 10925 on the same date, not earlier.
scope_check: Section 403 revokes EO 10733 by name and number as a whole, not a part; the same sentence abolishes the Committee whose membership EO 10733 amended, so both the preamble change and the paragraph (b) rewrite are covered.
independent_command_check: The two clauses are one command (increase membership from fifteen to sixteen and rewrite paragraph (b) to add an Executive Vice Chairman); there is no independent command, no deadline and no reporting duty.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued per the section 403 transfer of the Committee's records and property; nothing else is saved.
